why: wrong facts: Florida has no utility wind farms (EIA, 2025–26), and the Apalachicola River site is a hydroelectric dam (Jim Woodruff Dam, Florida’s only hydropower plant), not “pumps”; wind isn’t a growing source of Florida power
old: Florida uses both. The Sunshine State has wind farms along its coasts and hydroelectric pumps that move water at places like the Apalachicola River. Most of Florida's power still comes from natural gas, but more is coming from solar, wind, and water every year.
new: How does Florida use them? Sailboats ride the wind, and old farm windmills pumped water for cattle. Florida has almost no wind farms, because its usual winds are gentle. But one dam on the Apalachicola River, at the Georgia line, uses moving water to make electricity.
